subject: Order form commercial redlines — pricing staircase, invoicing cadence, net terms
messages:

Subject: Redwood order form draft and a few commercial questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Procurement and legal took an initial pass and asked that we clarify a few commercial items before we proceed to signature:

- Invoice cadence and acceptance criteria (Acme requires an invoice acceptance window for staged tranches).
- Net terms — our finance team typically requests Net 60 for new vendors in the onboarding year.
- How minimum commit tranches map to pricing bands (we want the waterfall spelled out).
- VAT/residency evidence for EU subsidiaries (we'll need a clause for reverse-charge when applicable).

Can you route to the appropriate teams at Redwood (legal + billing/finance) and share a redline summary? We can schedule a short call tomorrow if that's easier.

Thanks,
Maria López
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Dec 2029 08:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood order form draft and a few commercial questions

Thanks Jonas / Maria — attaching a redlined Order Form (RF_OrderForm_Redline_20291203.docx). High level summary of recommended positions and evidence asks: 

1) Net terms: Redwood standard is Net 30. For enterprise onboarding we can agree to Net 45 for the first 12 months, then revert to Net 30 thereafter. If Acme requires Net 60, we'll need an execution-level approval and a finance credit review (we can expedite but it will require a short underwriting step).

2) Minimum commit / pricing staircase: clarify the tranche mapping in Exhibit A. Suggested explicit language: initial tranche = $150,000 (upfront), then three quarterly tranches of $50,000 each (total annual commit $300,000). Pricing bands to step down by 8% once cumulative usage hits the second and third thresholds. We call out invoicing triggers for each tranche (activation vs. calendar quarter).

3) Invoicing / acceptance window: propose a 15-business-day invoice acceptance period for staged invoices; unpaid disputed line items do not hold undisputed amounts. Include PO reference on all invoices.

4) Taxes / VAT: For EU entities we will include a reverse-charge clause and ask Acme to provide VAT registration evidence per entity. For US invoicing, Redwood will remit gross amounts; Acme may claim VAT/exemption locally if appropriate. We mark required evidence in Section X (VAT certificates, tax IDs).

5) Audit/backup: add an optional clause that allows Acme to request billing backup for any invoice within 90 days (copy of usage report and invoice calculation).

Attachments: RF_OrderForm_Redline_20291203.docx (redline with tracked changes)

Action items:
- Jonas: confirm whether Acme will accept Net 45 for year 1 or will escalate to finance for Net 60 request.
- Ben: I'll defer to you for any credit/underwriting notes to include in DocuSign routing.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Dan Hsu <d.hsu@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Maria López <maria.lopez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Dec 2029 15:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood order form draft and a few commercial questions

Kimberly / Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. A couple of notes from Acme Legal / Procurement: 

- Acme prefers Net 60 during vendor onboarding as noted; however, we can accept Net 45 if Redwood's finance team confirms the underwriting/credit holdback is not required. Please confirm.
- The proposed tranche amounts look fine but Procurement asks that invoices be issued at the start of each quarter rather than on activation for tranche 2/3. Can you confirm invoice timing in the redline?
- VAT evidence: we'll prepare VAT certificates for EU entities; can you confirm the exact Section number where Redwood will list required evidence?

We ran your redline by procurement and legal. If Redwood can accept Net 45 for year one and issue invoices at quarter-start for tranches 2/3, we should be able to proceed to DocuSign. Sending a DocuSign link for signature in parallel so we don't lose momentum: https://app.docusign.com/some-doc-id-ACME-0042

Please confirm and we'll put this on procurement's queue for signature.

Best,
Dan Hsu
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
